Content:

\qquad s,t \in (-\infty,\infty).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by [MATH: \mathbf{r}=\mathbf{p}+ s\mathbf{b}+ t \mathbf{c},] where [MATH: \mathbf{p}] is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{b}] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point [MATH: P] is [MATH: \mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,5 \rangle,] and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are [MATH: \mathbf{b}= \langle 17,3,15 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}= \langle 5,0,-8 \rangle.]

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

[MATH: r|= ⟨ − 3, 2, 5⟩ + s⟨17, 3, 15⟩ + t⟨5, 0, − 8⟩, s, t ∈ (− ∞, ∞).]

sections.normalized_html: Find a normal vector to the plane [MATH: \mathbf{r}= \langle -6,3, 2 \rangle + t \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle + s \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle,\qquad t,\,s \in (-\infty,\infty).]
sections.readable_text:
Find a normal vector to the plane
[MATH: \mathbf{r}= \langle -6,3, 2 \rangle + t \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle + s \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle,\qquad t,\,s \in (-\infty,\infty).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
From the parametric equation, we have that [MATH: \mathbf{v} = \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{w} = \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle] are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of [MATH: \mathbf{v}] and [MATH: \mathbf{w}] as follows:

[MATH: n|= v × w; = [4; 2; − 1] × [4; − 3; 2]; = i|j|k; 4|2|− 1; 4|− 3|2; = i − 12j − 20k; = ⟨1, − 12, − 20⟩]

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is [MATH: \mathbf{n}=\langle 1, -12, -20 \rangle.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Any plane can be uniquely determined by a point and two non-parallel direction vectors. For example, let [MATH: \Pi] be the plane that passes through the point [MATH: P(1,0,2)] and is parallel to the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{b}= \langle 0,3,0 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}= \langle -1,1,1 \rangle.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f8fdab41563fd4a9a71cab6c587bb2fb]

Content:
Using the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{b}] and [MATH: \mathbf{c},] we can construct a parametric equation of the plane.

Content:
First, let [MATH: R] be any general point in the plane, with position vector [MATH: \mathbf{r}.] Notice that we can get from [MATH: P] to [MATH: R] using a linear combination of [MATH: \mathbf{b}] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] with some (unknown for us) coefficients [MATH: s] and [MATH: t], as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/34379adabad0df3c0aefa5b60edc5007]

Content:
So, we can write the parametric equation of the plane as

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}\mathbf{r}} = \mathbf{p}+s{\color{blue}\,\mathbf{b}}+t\,{\color{blue}\mathbf{c}},
\qquad s,t \in (-\infty,\infty).]

Content:
This formula works whenever [MATH: \mathbf{b}] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] are not parallel.

Content:
In our case, [MATH: \mathbf{b}] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] are indeed not parallel to each other. So, using column vector notation, the parametric equation for the plane [MATH: \Pi] is given by
[MATH: [1; 0; 2]]

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Given Vectors

Example Prompt:
Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point [MATH: P(-3,2,5)] and is parallel to the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{b}= \langle 17,3,15 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}= \langle 5,0,-8 \rangle.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
A parametric equation of a plane is given by
[MATH: \mathbf{r}=\mathbf{p}+ s\mathbf{b}+ t \mathbf{c},]
where [MATH: \mathbf{p}] is the position vector of a point on the plane and the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{b}] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

Here, the position vector of the given point [MATH: P] is [MATH: \mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,5 \rangle,] and the two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other) are [MATH: \mathbf{b}= \langle 17,3,15 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{c}= \langle 5,0,-8 \rangle.]

So, a parametric equation of the plane is given by

[MATH: r|= ⟨ − 3, 2, 5⟩ + s⟨17, 3, 15⟩ + t⟨5, 0, − 8⟩, s, t ∈ (− ∞, ∞).]

---

Item 5 — Example: Finding a Normal Vector To a Plane Given by Parametric Equation

Example Prompt:
Find a normal vector to the plane
[MATH: \mathbf{r}= \langle -6,3, 2 \rangle + t \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle + s \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle,\qquad t,\,s \in (-\infty,\infty).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
From the parametric equation, we have that [MATH: \mathbf{v} = \langle 4, 2, -1 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{w} = \langle 4, -3, 2 \rangle] are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of [MATH: \mathbf{v}] and [MATH: \mathbf{w}] as follows:

[MATH: n|= v × w; = [4; 2; − 1] × [4; − 3; 2]; = i|j|k; 4|2|− 1; 4|− 3|2; = i − 12j − 20k; = ⟨1, − 12, − 20⟩]

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is [MATH: \mathbf{n}=\langle 1, -12, -20 \rangle.]
